subject: Private offer: multisku pricing + reseller pass-through request from CloudFirm
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@cloudfirm.io>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurements@cloudfirm.io
Date: 2028-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Multi-sku private offer & reseller margin pass-through

Hi Sergio —

Thanks for taking this. CloudFirm is preparing an internal ask for a private offer across two SKUs (reserved capacity node-hours + metered inference tokens/embeddings). High level: we are targeting a single blended discount off list (~35%) across the commit and metered usage, and we need a clean reseller pass-through to our partner PartnerEdge at 10% (they will handle local invoicing).

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood can support a blended private offer that spans reserved node commits + metered tokens under one PO
- How reseller pass-through is handled in the invoice and whether Redwood issues a split invoice line for the partner
- What evidence you need from PartnerEdge to enable automatic pass-through (W-9/EIN equivalent, reseller agreement, invoice routing)
- Any tax or marketplace constraints we should plan for if this needs to be listed as a private offer in AWS Marketplace

Goal: get term sheet (SKU-level mapping + price) this week so our procurement can circulate.

Cheers,
Elena Park
Head of Cloud Ops, CloudFirm
procurements@cloudfirm.io

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@cloudfirm.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-sku private offer & reseller margin pass-through

Elena —

Appreciate the detail. Short answers up front: yes, we can do a blended private offer across commit + metered SKUs; and yes, we support reseller pass-through, but there are a couple of packaging/ops choices that change how it shows up on invoices and what evidence we require.

Options we usually propose:
- Blended single-line PO: simplifies procurement but requires us to map internal SKU allocation for revenue recognition; reseller pass-through is applied as a post-invoice credit to PartnerEdge (visible on our side).
- SKU-level pricing: separate prices for reserved node-hours (commit) and metered tokens, with explicit pass-through % on the SKU line so PartnerEdge can see it directly on their invoice copy.

From an ask perspective, please share a 12-month expected usage profile (reserve vs metered %) and the PartnerEdge partner ID or contact. Ben (channel ops) and Camila (deal ops) are cc'd — they'll scope the evidence checklist and get a PO template over. I attached a brief pricing workbook template to capture usage buckets.

Next step: if you can drop usage by Wednesday, Ben will confirm required reseller docs and Camila will push a draft PO/DocuSign for signature.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com

On Tue, May 1, 2028 at 11:05 AM sergio_alvarez@redwood.com wrote:
> From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
> Appreciate the detail. Short answers up front: yes, we can do a blended private offer...

Elena —

Quick channel/ops clarifiers from my side:
- Pass-through models we support:
  1) Partner self-invoices downstream: Redwood invoices CloudFirm at net (after partner passback) and we provide partner payout details to your partner finance team.
  2) Redwood invoices gross and issues a separate remit/credit to PartnerEdge (shows as separate credit line).
  3) AWS Marketplace private-offer routing: if we route via marketplace, the pass-through mechanics and tax handling differ (Marketplace takes responsibility for remitting funds in some geos).

- Typical pass-through % we see is 8–12% for distributors/resellers on private offers; 10% is reasonable but we need the partner contract or broker ID to automate.
- Required evidence: partner W-9 or local tax doc, reseller agreement or letter of appointment, and preferred invoice routing (email + remit-to). If PartnerEdge wants net remittance directly, we will need a signed reseller agreement and invoice routing form.

I attached our reseller_evidence_checklist.pdf — Camila, can you draft a PO with two scenarios (blended vs sku-level) so CloudFirm can pick?

Ben Carter
Channel Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@cloudfirm.io>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-02T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-sku private offer & reseller margin pass-through

Good morning —

Thanks, Elena. I've sketched two concrete price structures in the attached pricing_workbook.xlsx and a PO template for each path. Summary of the proposal: 

Scenario A (preferred for procurement simplicity):
- Single blended discount: 34% off list across the two SKUs
- Redwood issues a single PO/Invoice to CloudFirm; Redwood posts an automated payout to PartnerEdge (10% of gross) as a separate remit line.

Scenario B (preferred for partner transparency):
- SKU-level pricing: Reserved node-hours = 30% off list; Metered tokens/embeddings = 40% off list
- PartnerEdge pass-through = 10% on gross for each SKU; partner sees explicit line items on their invoice copy.

Requirements to enable Scenario A automation: signed reseller appointment + remit-to details (email and ACH/wiring info) and a short statement of reseller commission. For Scenario B we need the same docs but they can be attached directly to the marketplace private-offer config.

DocuSign link for the PO (draft) is here: https://app.docusign.com/rooms/abc123-cloudfirm-po
Pricing workbook (details): https://d.docs.redwood.com/pricing/rdw-1739-workbook

If CloudFirm is comfortable with Scenario A at 34% blended, we'll mark that as the default and prepare the DocuSign for signature. Otherwise pick Scenario B and indicate whether the partner needs separate invoice lines.

Camila Reyes
Deal Operations | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com

From: Elena Park <elena@cloudfirm.io>

Subject: Re: Multi-sku private offer & reseller margin pass-through

Thanks, team. Helpful options — procurement prefers a single blended line (simpler for PO routing). A couple follow-ups: 

- Does Redwood produce an invoice that has a separate remit/credit to PartnerEdge (we need that to reconcile partner payouts) or would PartnerEdge receive a separate invoice from Redwood?
- PartnerEdge has requested Redwood's reseller SOC2 excerpt (they perform partner security reviews). Will you accept a partner-facing excerpt, or do we need to include PartnerEdge directly in a Redwood security evidence request?
- Final ask: can you show a sample invoice with the 34% blended and a 10% partner payout line? Procurement needs to see the flow before we sign.

If you can send sample invoice + the PO DocuSign by EOD, we can get internal approval next morning.

Elena

On Thu, May 2, 2028 at 10:15 AM Elena Park <elena@cloudfirm.io> wrote:
> Thanks, team. Helpful options — procurement prefers a single blended line (simpler for PO routing)...

Elena —

We can do a blended 34% off list and show PartnerEdge as a separate payout line on the invoice (example attached in the pricing workbook). PartnerEdge will not receive a separate invoice from Redwood by default; instead Redwood issues gross invoice to CloudFirm and posts a separate payable to PartnerEdge (visible on finance export and partner reporting). If PartnerEdge needs a standalone invoice, we can coordinate to generate one but that adds ops steps.

Re: SOC2 excerpt — yes, we can provide a partner-facing SOC2 summary and a link to our security evidence portal. If PartnerEdge wants direct access, we can create a short evidence share but will need a partner contact and an NDA addendum (if required).

Next steps:
1) Camila will send the DocuSign PO for 34% blended (she's attached a draft).
2) Ben will email the reseller evidence checklist to PartnerEdge and request remit info.
3) Elena, once you confirm PartnerEdge contact and signing authority, we'll push the private offer into the AWS marketplace (if you want marketplace routing) or keep it off-marketplace and invoice directly.

I'll set a 20-minute wrap-up call if you'd like to run the invoice sample with your finance team.

—Sergio
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
